messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: runtime-prod-1 continuous-batching KV cache reuse error spike detected. 5xxs up 23% in last 5m, p95 latency +120ms. Possible KV cache cross-request reuse. Details: metric=kvcache.reuse_error rate=0.18; samples: request_id=[a1,b2,c3].

devon (oncall): Seeing the same in traces. A subset of chat sessions show stale seq offsets and wrong KV hits — responses with previous user context. Paging up.

margo: Paging in eng-runtime and eng-sre. Oncall handoff incoming in ~20m. Any quick mitigations before rotation?

ryan: Can we flip continuous-batching -> disable for runtime-prod-1 only? That's the highest-risk knob.

devon (oncall): I can hotpatch a config change to disable continuous-batching on that pool. Will run a canary to 5% first.

carol: Also recommend flushing KV caches for affected workers after the change to avoid stale entries being reused.

infra-bot: Suggested command: `kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deploy/inference-pool-prod-1` — this will drop KV caches. Use during low traffic.

devon (oncall): Executing canary disable now. Patch: `PATCH /config/pools/prod-1 {"continuous_batching": false}`. Applying to 1 of 10 nodes.

ryan: Copy that. I'm preparing a script to flush per-worker caches via admin API:
```
for pod in $(kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=inference-pool-prod-1 -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
  curl -X POST http://$pod:8080/admin/kv/flush
done
```

devon (oncall): Canary returned: metrics down 40% for reuse_error on that node but p95 latency bumped slightly. No 5xx increase so far. Scaling canary to 30% now.

louise (cs): Heads up — two customers (gamma-data, atlas-ai) reported contextual bleed in sessions. We're flagging them and sending interim guidance: restart sessions, temporarily disable long-lived chats.

carol: We're seeing specific failure pattern in logs: `kvcache.lookup: hit but seq_mismatch expected=124 got=117` and `kvcache.owner: request_id mismatch`. Looks like stale seq offsets are being re-used across requests.

devon (oncall): Root theory: cache entries keyed by (model, session_id) but a bug in the sharding code used a stale seq_base when promoting partial KV entries during continuous batching. When requests race, offsets from previous requests were written back and then read by the next request.

sre-rotation: Start an immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable continuous-batching on prod-1 (in flight) 2) restart pool pods to force cache flush (scheduled) 3) patch key composition to include request_seq_base until proper fix 4) revert once validated.

ryan: I'm pushing a short-term config hotfix to augment keys with `seq_epoch` (derived from worker restart counter). That will avoid cross-request hits until we fix promotion logic. Patch PR: `eng-runtime#2573`.

devon (oncall): Hotfix rolled to prod-1 nodes at 18:25 UTC. Flushing caches across pool now. Running smoke evals against a set of replay prompts.

devon (oncall): Smoke evals: 100 prompts, before: 7/100 with bleed; after canary+flush+hotfix: 1/100. Metrics trending toward baseline.

louise (cs): Updating customers: telling them we've applied mitigation and are monitoring. Asking for any new examples. They're appreciative of quick response.

carol: Starting deeper investigation into the promotion path that writes partial KV segments during batching. Reproduced locally with concurrent replay harness. Repro: send 3 overlapping requests with differing seq offsets and assert keys written with mismatched offsets.

ryan: Noted a suspicious change in the batching kernel from last release: `batch_promote()` had a refactor that removed an atomic copy of seq_base in favor of a shared pointer — likely source of race. Opening revert PR.

devon (oncall): Handoff note for next oncall (sre-rotation): mitigation completed for prod-1, continuous-batching disabled, per-worker flush done, hotfix applied to key composition. We'll keep continuous-batching off until patch is merged + validated across other pools.

sre-rotation: Acknowledged. Adding follow-ups: 1) cross-pool sweep to check for similar reuse_error spikes 2) roll a full rollout of hotfix after regression tests 3) add unit tests for seq_base atomicity and a stress test.

carol: For postmortem — capture timeline, root cause (race in batch_promote writing seq offset), impact (context bleed for some customer sessions, up to 23% 5xx for a subset), mitigation steps, and long-term fix (ensure copy-on-write in promotion; additional invariants).

louise (cs): Customers updated: gamma-data had 4 sessions affected, atlas-ai 2 sessions. No PII leak observed. Offering credits and postmortem.

devon (oncall): Metrics check at +30m: reuse_error dropped to baseline (0.02), p95 latency normalized. Continuous-batching off on prod-1. Will coordinate gradual rollout of fix to prod-2/3 after tests pass.

ryan: Plan to backfill a regression suite that runs the concurrent-replay harness against every PR touching batching/promotion. Also adding a CI job that fuzzes seq offsets for 1h per merge.

sre-rotation: Adding action items to incident board: (a) revert risky refactor or add atomic fix (b) rollout hotfix to other regions (c) update runbooks for KV cache flush and disabling batching (d) customer comms review.

devon (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated. Will leave thread pinned for postmortem notes. Thanks everyone for quick responses :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity=sev2, status=mitigated, incident_id=INC-2024-0731, owner=devon (oncall), start_ts=1854326789, mitigated_ts=1854330389
